text.p: Inspired pace bowling from Darren Gough helped England claw their way back into the match on the third day of the second test at Harare Sports Club.
After losing the morning session due to a damp outfield Zimbabwe struggled from their overnight 93 for two to 155 for six at tea, with Gough taking three of the wickets to fall.

Gough provided the key early breakthrough when he had Zimbabwe player-coach Dave Houghton caught down the leg side in his first over. Houghton had scored 29 from 123 balls in a stand of 64 with Grant Flower for the third wicket.

Flower lost his younger brother Andy to a swinging yorker from Gough with the score on 131. Flower looked unfortunate to be given lbw by Russell Tiffin for six but not as unfortunate as Andy Waller five runs later.
This time it was Sri Lankan umpire K.T. Francis who upheld a shout from Phil Tufnell. Waller played no shot to a ball from the left-arm spinner which looked clearly to be missing off stump.
But there was no fortune involved in the next dismissal. Gough beat Guy Whittall for pace and ripped out his leg stump when the all-rounder had scored a single.
Zimbabwe's main hope of a big first innings lead now lies with Grant Flower who has so far carried his bat for 69 from 248 balls with four fours and a six.
